description: Start a website crawl job from a seed URL. Crawls pages breadth-first (BFS) up to the 'depth' parameter (BFS levels from the seed) and the 'limit' parameter (maximum number of pages to crawl). Supports Markdown and HTML output formats, optional JavaScript rendering, proxy geo-targeting, domain filtering, and the grouped wait_config browser wait policy. Omit wait_config or set it to null to keep adaptive browser settling for page extractions; send {} or concrete values to opt every page extraction into explicit mode. Returns a job ID that can be polled with the 'crawl_status' tool. Requires a Geonode API key, sent as the X-Api-Key header.

depth.description: Maximum BFS depth from the seed URL (1 = seed only)
depth.title: Depth

formats.description: Output formats to extract per page
formats.title: Formats

include_subdomains.description: When same_domain_only is true, also include subdomains of the seed domain
include_subdomains.title: Include Subdomains

limit.description: Maximum number of pages to crawl
limit.title: Limit

proxy.description: Proxy configuration for page requests. Optional — when omitted or explicitly `null`, defaults are applied per page: residential type, country auto-resolved from each page URL (domain/path overrides first, then the TLD; if nothing matches, the upstream proxy provider picks the exit region). Send an object to override either field; individual fields inside the object may also be null (see ProxySettings).

render_js.description: Use a headless browser to render each page (slower, handles JS-heavy sites)
render_js.title: Render Js

same_domain_only.description: Only follow links that stay on the same domain as the seed URL
same_domain_only.title: Same Domain Only

url.description: Seed URL to start crawling from
url.title: Url

wait_config.description: Grouped browser wait policy applied to every crawled page extraction. Optional — when omitted or explicitly `null`, each page extraction uses the adaptive default settle policy whenever a browser runs. Send an object to opt every page extraction into caller-owned explicit wait mode, which skips the adaptive default settle phase. Only non-null wait_config values count as provided; null fields inside wait_config behave the same as absence. If render_js is not set explicitly, any non-null wait_config value auto-enables browser rendering for the workflow and the effective render_js value is returned in crawl_config. If you explicitly send render_js=false together with non-null wait_config values, the request is rejected as ambiguous.

country.description: ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 country code for geo-targeting (e.g., 'US', 'GB'). Codes that are not backed by a geo-targeted proxy pool are rejected rather than silently ignored. If null, the server auto-resolves a country from the target URL (domain/path overrides first, then the TLD). If no country can be inferred, the upstream proxy provider picks the exit region.
country.title: Country

type.description: Type of proxy to use (datacenter or residential). Defaults to 'residential' when omitted.

WaitConfig.description:
Explicit browser wait policy applied in order: wait_until → wait_for → wait_timeout.
When a non-null WaitConfig is provided, the adaptive default settle phase is skipped
and the caller owns the full wait sequence. Null fields inside the object are treated
the same as absence of that field.

wait_for.description: CSS selector or XPath expression to wait for before extracting the DOM. At least one matching element must become attached to the DOM for the wait to succeed. XPath expressions must start with `//` or `xpath=`; anything else is treated as a CSS selector. Applied after wait_until.
wait_for.title: Wait For

wait_timeout.description: Deliberate pause in milliseconds inserted after wait_for resolves (or immediately after wait_until when wait_for is omitted), before the DOM is captured. Use to allow late-settling JavaScript to finish rendering. Range: 0–30 000 ms.
wait_timeout.title: Wait Timeout

wait_until.description: Playwright page lifecycle event to wait for during navigation, before the selector wait or explicit delay. Accepted values: `commit` — response headers received and navigation committed; `domcontentloaded` — HTML parsed and DOM ready (no sub-resources); `load` — page and all sub-resources (images, scripts) fully loaded; `networkidle` — no network activity for 500 ms. When omitted, defaults to `domcontentloaded`.

WaitConfig.title: WaitConfig

name: crawl
title: Start a site crawl
